text: To find the center of a given circle. Let $ABC$ be the given circle. So it is required to find the center of circle $ABC$.
Let some straight-line $AB$ be drawn through ($ABC$), at random,
and let ($AB$) be cut in half at point $D$ [Prop.~1.9].
And let $DC$ be drawn from $D$, at right-angles to $AB$ [Prop.~1.11].
And let ($CD$) be drawn through to $E$.
And let $CE$ be cut in half at $F$ [Prop.~1.9].
I say that (point) $F$ is the center of the [circle] $ABC$.
For (if) not (then), if possible, let $G$ (be the center of the circle),
assertion: G is supposed to be the center (supposition for contradiction)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: let $G$ (be the center of the circle)

text: and let $GA$, $GD$, and $GB$ be joined.
And since $AD$ is equal to $DB$, and $DG$ (is) common, the two (straight-lines) $AD$, $DG$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BD$, $DG$,$^\dag$ respectively.
assertion: the two straight-lines AD, DG are equal to the two straight-lines BD, DG respectively

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the two (straight-lines) $AD$, $DG$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BD$, $DG$,$^\dag$ respectively

text: And the base $GA$ is equal to the base $GB$. For (they are both) radii.
assertion: base GA equals base GB (they are both radii)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the base $GA$ is equal to the base $GB$

text: Thus, angle $ADG$ is equal to angle $GDB$ [Prop.~1.8].
And when a straight-line stood upon (another) straight-line make adjacent angles (which are) equal to one another, each of the equal angles is a right-angle [Def.~1.10].
assertion: each of the equal adjacent angles is a right-angle

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: a straight-line stood upon (another) straight-line make adjacent angles (which are) equal to one another

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: each of the equal angles is a right-angle

text: Thus, $GDB$ is a right-angle.
And $FDB$ is also a right-angle.
Thus, $FDB$ (is) equal to $GDB$, the greater to the lesser.
assertion: FDB equals GDB (the greater to the lesser, which is absurd)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $FDB$ (is) equal to $GDB$, the greater to the lesser

text: The very thing is impossible.
Thus, (point) $G$ is not the center of the circle $ABC$.
assertion: G is not the center of circle ABC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (point) $G$ is not the center of the circle $ABC$

text: So, similarly, we can show that neither is any other (point) except $F$.
assertion: no other point except F can be the center of circle ABC

spans.text: So, similarly, we can show that

text: Thus, point $F$ is the center of the [circle] $ABC$.
assertion: F is the center of circle ABC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: point $F$ is the center of the [circle] $ABC$

text: So, from this, (it is) manifest that if any straight-line in a circle cuts any (other) straight-line in half, and at right-angles, (then) the center of the circle is on the former (straight-line).
assertion: if a straight-line bisects another at right-angles in a circle, the center is on the bisecting line (porism)
